title: Everyday Statistics: Pictograms, Bar Charts, Mode and Chance
seo_title: Everyday Statistics – Primary 4 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Collect and present data in pictograms and bar charts; find the mode of a set of data; describe the chance of simple events. (summary of the NERDC Primary 4 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free Primary 4 maths worksheets on everyday statistics: reading pictograms and bar charts, finding the mode, and describing chance as impossible, unlikely, likely or certain. 100 questions with answers.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A pictogram uses pictures to show data. Always read the key: one picture may stand for 2, 5 or 10 things.
  • A bar chart uses bars. Read the height of each bar on the scale.
  • The mode is the value that appears most often.
  • Chance describes how likely something is: impossible, unlikely, equally likely, likely or certain.

Examples

Example

Scores 4, 7, 4, 9, 4, 6

4 appears 3 times

Answer: Mode = 4

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Ignoring the key in a pictogramMultiply the number of pictures by what one picture stands for.
Giving how many times, not the valueThe mode is the value, not how often it appears.
Thinking unlikely means impossibleUnlikely things can still happen.

faq.a: Facts and numbers we collect, such as favourite foods.

items.q: How many sparrows were seen?
items.e: Look at the key: each circle stands for 2 birds. The Sparrow row has 6 circles: 6 × 2 = 12 birds.
Look at the key: each star stands for 5 cakes. The Mon row has 5 stars: 5 × 5 = 25 cakes.

items.q: How many points did Hawk House get?
items.e: Look at the key: each square stands for 10 points. The Hawk row has 4 squares and half a square: 4 × 10 = 40, and half of 10 is 5, so 40 + 5 = 45 points.

items.q: In this pictogram, what does half a circle stand for?
items.e: The key says one whole circle = 10 lollies. Half a circle is half of 10, which is 5 lollies, not 1.
Look at the key: each star stands for 5 votes. The Apple row has 2 stars: 2 × 5 = 10 votes.

items.q: Which row shows the most stickers?
items.e: Every square stands for the same number, so the row with the most squares shows the most. The Kayode row has 6 squares: 6 × 2 = 12 stickers.

items.q: Each star stands for 2 books. Uju read 9 books. How many stars should be in her row?
items.e: Count in 2s: 2, 4, 6, 8. 4 whole stars make 8. 1 more is half of 2, so add half a star. Draw 4 and a half stars.
Look at the key: each star stands for 2 votes. The Blue row has 5 stars and half a star: 5 × 2 = 10, and half of 2 is 1, so 10 + 1 = 11 votes.

items.q: In this pictogram, what does half a square stand for?
items.e: The key says one whole square = 10 books. Half a square is half of 10, which is 5 books, not 1.

items.q: Which row shows 7 pupils?
items.e: Half a circle is 1, so 7 pupils is 3 and a half circles. The Cricket row has 3 circles and half a circle: 3 × 2 = 6, and half of 2 is 1, so 6 + 1 = 7 pupils.
Look at the key: each star stands for 10 cans. The 3A row has 4 stars and half a star: 4 × 10 = 40, and half of 10 is 5, so 40 + 5 = 45 cans.

items.q: Which row shows the fewest minibeasts?
items.e: Every square stands for the same number, so the row with the fewest squares shows the fewest. The Ladybird row has 1 square: 1 × 5 = 5 minibeasts.

items.q: Each circle stands for 10 pupils. 45 pupils walk to school. How many circles should be in the Walk row?
items.e: Count in 10s: 10, 20, 30, 40. 4 whole circles make 40. 5 more is half of 10, so add half a circle. Draw 4 and a half circles.
Look at the key: each star stands for 5 books. The Ikenna row has 6 stars: 6 × 5 = 30 books.

items.q: How many pupils have a fish?
items.e: Look at the key: each square stands for 2 pupils. The Fish row has 1 square and half a square: 1 × 2 = 2, and half of 2 is 1, so 2 + 1 = 3 pupils.

items.q: In this pictogram, what does half a circle stand for?
items.e: The key says one whole circle = 10 pupils. Half a circle is half of 10, which is 5 pupils, not 1.
Half a star is 5, so 35 cakes is 3 and a half stars. The Tue row has 3 stars and half a star: 3 × 10 = 30, and half of 10 is 5, so 30 + 5 = 35 cakes.

items.q: How many shells did Femi find?
items.e: Look at the key: each square stands for 5 shells. The Femi row has 5 squares: 5 × 5 = 25 shells.

items.q: Each square stands for 5 votes. Red got 30 votes. How many squares should be in the Red row?
items.e: Count in 5s until you reach 30: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30. That is 6 steps, so draw 6 squares. Check: 6 × 5 = 30.
Look at the key: each star stands for 10 books. The Mystery row has 4 stars and half a star: 4 × 10 = 40, and half of 10 is 5, so 40 + 5 = 45 books.

items.q: What does the scale on this bar chart go up in?
items.e: Read the numbers on the scale: 0, 2, 4, 6 … Each line is 2 more than the one before, so the scale goes up in 2s.

items.q: How many cakes were sold on Wednesday?
items.e: The scale goes up in 2s. The Wed bar ends on the line for 4. So the answer is 4 cakes.

items.q: How many pupils come by scooter to school?
items.e: The scale goes up in 5s. The Scooter bar ends on the line for 10. So the answer is 10 pupils.

items.q: How many pupils chose swimming?
items.e: The scale goes up in 10s. The Swimming bar ends halfway between 10 and 20, so it shows 15. So the answer is 15 pupils.

items.q: How many blue tits were seen?
items.e: The scale goes up in 2s. The Blue tit bar ends on the line for 2. So the answer is 2 birds.

items.q: Which bar shows 30 books?
items.e: The scale goes up in 5s. Find 30 on the scale. The Uju bar ends on the line for 30.

items.q: How many points did Falcon House get?
items.e: The scale goes up in 10s. The Falcon bar ends halfway between 60 and 70, so it shows 65. So the answer is 65 points.

items.q: What does the scale on this bar chart go up in?
items.e: Read the numbers on the scale: 0, 5, 10, 15 … Each line is 5 more than the one before, so the scale goes up in 5s.

items.q: Which bar shows the most votes?
items.e: The Orange bar is the tallest one. The Orange bar ends on the line for 14. It shows 14 votes.

items.q: How many cans did class 3A collect?
items.e: The scale goes up in 10s. The 3A bar ends halfway between 50 and 60, so it shows 55. So the answer is 55 cans.

items.q: How many snails were found?
items.e: The scale goes up in 5s. The Snail bar ends on the line for 20. So the answer is 20 minibeasts.

items.q: How many shells did Ngozi find?
items.e: The scale goes up in 2s. The Ngozi bar ends halfway between 12 and 14, so it shows 13. So the answer is 13 shells.

items.q: Which bar shows the fewest books?
items.e: The Sport bar is the shortest one. The Sport bar ends on the line for 10. It shows 10 books.

items.q: How many cola lollies were sold?
items.e: The scale goes up in 5s. The Cola bar ends on the line for 35. So the answer is 35 lollies.

items.q: How many pupils have a rabbit?
items.e: The scale goes up in 2s. The Rabbit bar ends halfway between 10 and 12, so it shows 11. So the answer is 11 pupils.

items.q: Which bar shows 25 cans?
items.e: The scale goes up in 10s. Find 25 on the scale. The 3A bar ends halfway between 20 and 30, so it shows 25.

items.q: How many pupils chose rugby?
items.e: The scale goes up in 10s. The Rugby bar ends on the line for 60. So the answer is 60 pupils.

items.q: Which bar shows the most stickers?
items.e: The Joy bar is the tallest one. The Joy bar ends on the line for 35. It shows 35 stickers.

items.q: How many pupils have a rabbit?
items.e: The scale goes up in 2s. The Rabbit bar ends halfway between 6 and 8, so it shows 7. So the answer is 7 pupils.

items.q: Which bar shows 4 votes?
items.e: The scale goes up in 2s. Find 4 on the scale. The Purple bar ends on the line for 4.

items.q: What is the mode of these scores: 7, 6, 7, 9, 4, 1, 4, 6, 4?
items.e: The mode is the number that appears most often. 4 appears 3 times: 4.

items.q: What is the mode of these scores: 4, 5, 1, 7, 1, 9, 11, 8?
items.e: The mode is the number that appears most often. 1 appears 2 times: 1.

items.q: What is the mode of these scores: 10, 3, 2, 9, 11, 11, 3, 6, 4, 3?
items.e: The mode is the number that appears most often. 3 appears 3 times: 3.

items.q: What is the mode of these scores: 6, 11, 2, 7, 11, 3, 8, 12?

items.q: What is the mode of these scores: 7, 8, 1, 4, 1, 2, 8, 3, 2, 8, 10?

items.q: What is the mode of these scores: 7, 1, 3, 4, 3, 9, 3, 3, 9?

items.q: What is the mode of these scores: 8, 12, 1, 8, 6, 1, 5, 12, 12?
items.e: The mode is the number that appears most often. 12 appears 3 times: 12.

items.q: How likely is this? A goat will fly to school.
items.e: Impossible.

items.q: How likely is this? The sun will rise in the east tomorrow.
items.e: Certain.

items.q: How likely is this? You will pick a blue ball from a bag with 9 red balls and 1 blue ball.
items.e: Unlikely.

items.q: How likely is this? You will roll an even number on a dice.
items.e: Equally likely.

items.q: How likely is this? It will rain in Kano in July.
items.e: Likely.

items.q: How likely is this? It will rain somewhere in Nigeria during the rainy season.
items.e: Certain.

items.q: How likely is this? You will pick a red ball from a bag of only blue balls.
items.e: Impossible.

items.q: How likely is this? A baby will be born somewhere in Nigeria today.
items.e: Certain.

items.q: How likely is this? You will pick a red ball from a bag with 9 red balls and 1 blue ball.
items.e: Likely.

items.q: How likely is this? A tossed coin will land on heads.
items.e: Equally likely.

items.q: The sun will rise tomorrow morning. This is …
items.e: The sun rises every morning. It always happens, so it is certain.

items.q: After Wednesday, the next day will be Thursday. This is …
items.e: The days of the week always come in the same order. Thursday always comes after Wednesday, so it is certain.

items.q: Kelechi is 8. Next year he will be 9. This is …
items.e: Everyone is one year older each year. 8 + 1 = 9, so it is certain.

items.q: Tomorrow will have 30 hours. This is …
items.e: Every day has 24 hours. A day can never have 30 hours, so it is impossible.

items.q: If Amaka drops a tennis ball, it will fall down. This is …
items.e: When you let go of a ball, it always falls to the ground. It must happen, so it is certain.

items.q: Yusuf is 8. Next year he will be 3 years old. This is …
items.e: You cannot get younger. Next year Yusuf will be 9, so being 3 is impossible.

items.q: The next vehicle that drives past the school will have 4 wheels. This is …
items.e: Most vehicles on the road are cars with 4 wheels. But the next one could be a motorbike or a truck, so it is likely, not certain.

items.q: Joy will drink some water at school today. This is …
items.e: Most pupils drink water during a school day. Joy could forget, so it is likely, not certain.

items.q: Dayo will roll a 6 on a dice five times in a row. This is …
items.e: Rolling a 6 once is unlikely (1 out of 6 faces). Five 6s in a row is even harder. It could happen, so it is unlikely, not impossible.

items.q: Which event is certain?
c: Kayode will have pasta for dinner
Ngozi will win her race at the athletics carnival
items.e: Friday always comes after Thursday, so it is certain. Rain, winning a race and pasta for dinner might happen, but they might not.

items.q: The spinner has 4 equal sections. Which colour is the arrow most likely to land on?
c: red and blue are equally likely
items.e: 3 of the 4 equal sections are red and only 1 is blue, so red is most likely. (There is no green, so green is impossible.)

items.q: The spinner has 6 equal sections. Which colour is the arrow least likely to land on?
items.e: Only 1 of the 6 equal sections is green. 5 are yellow. Green has the smallest part, so it is least likely.

items.q: Landing on red is …
items.e: Every section is red. The arrow must land on red, so it is certain.

items.q: Landing on red is …
items.e: Only 1 of the 6 equal sections is red. It can happen, but not often, so it is unlikely. It is not impossible, because there is a red section.

items.q: Landing on green is …
items.e: There is no green section on this spinner. The arrow can never land on green, so it is impossible.

items.q: Landing on green is …
items.e: 5 of the 6 equal sections are green, so green is likely. It is not certain, because there is 1 purple section.

items.q: Which colour can the arrow never land on?
items.e: The spinner has red, blue and yellow sections only. There is no green, so landing on green is impossible.

items.q: Which colour is the arrow most likely to land on?
c: all three colours are equally likely
items.e: Look at the size of each part, not the number of sections. Blue is one big section: half of the spinner. Red is 2 small sections (a quarter) and yellow is 2 small sections (a quarter). So blue is most likely.

items.q: Which two colours are equally likely?
items.e: Red and green are each a quarter of the spinner. Parts of the same size are equally likely. Yellow is half of the spinner, so it is more likely than red or green.

items.q: Landing on yellow is …
items.e: Yellow is only a quarter of the spinner and green is three quarters. Yellow can happen, but it is unlikely.

items.q: Zainab picks one counter from the bag without looking. Which colour is she most likely to pick?
c: red and blue are equally likely
items.e: There are 6 red counters and only 2 blue counters. More red counters means red is more likely.

items.q: Victor picks one counter without looking. Which colour is he least likely to pick?
items.e: There is only 1 green counter and 7 yellow counters, so green is least likely.

items.q: Picking a blue counter from this bag is …
items.e: Every counter in the bag is blue, so you must pick blue. It is certain.

items.q: Picking a green counter from this bag is …
items.e: There are only red and yellow counters. There is no green counter, so it is impossible.

items.q: Picking a red counter from this bag is …
items.e: 7 of the 8 counters are red, so red is likely. It is not certain, because there is 1 blue counter.

items.q: Picking a red counter from this bag is …
items.e: Only 1 of the 10 counters is red. It can happen, but not often, so it is unlikely, not impossible.

items.q: Which colour is impossible to pick from this bag?
items.e: The bag has red, blue and yellow counters. There is no green, so green is impossible. There is 1 yellow counter, so yellow is unlikely, not impossible.

items.q: Which sentence is true?
c: Red is more likely than blue
Red and blue are equally likely
items.e: There are 4 red and 4 blue counters. The same number of each colour means they are equally likely.

items.q: This bag has 9 green marbles and 1 purple marble. Bisi picks one marble without looking. Picking the purple marble is …
items.e: Only 1 of the 10 marbles is purple. It can happen, but it is unlikely.

items.q: Which two colours are equally likely to be picked?
items.e: There are 3 red, 3 blue and 2 yellow counters. Red and blue have the same number, so they are equally likely.
